thesis: The answer that cost a Kodiak hunter $150 sat on top of a stack of summaries, and the one binding text, the state's regulation, is what she opened to find the right date and turn herself in.
supporting_facts: c4/c5/c8: opening the regs is how she found Oct 8 and self-reported
c6: the trooper ran the identical search and got the identical wrong answer, so the error repeats for every searcher
c13+c15: even ADF&G calls its online regs simplified, and Google's own page says check more than one place
counterpoint_to_honor: Google's warning and the state's rule both existed and she still paid $150; but a wrong answer that replicates for every searcher (c6) and that DPS expects to see again (c9,c11) is not one hunter's slip. Nothing in the file says what the AI cited, so no claim about Google's sourcing.
falsifiability: False if the trooper's identical search had returned a correct date, or if ADF&G's own published listing said Sept 1 (the booklet did not load, so this is disclosed as unverified).
second_movement: c13 recontextualizes the 'one source of truth' line: it is itself a simplified convenience over the statute, so the honest lesson is a stack of summaries over one binding text, not AI bad and the official page good.
valence: mixed, respectful of Weaver, constructive, no scold, no pile-on at Google
runner_ups: Honesty as the working safeguard (self-report + replication)
Provenance ask: AI answers that name the ADF&G source (booklet did not load so the falsifier is open)
why_runner_ups_lost: each is a sub-beat of the chosen thesis; the provenance ask overreaches the evidence (nothing says what the AI cited)
